<Heading
  as={"h1"}

  children={"Start an associate's shift"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/associates/{id}/shift-starts"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Creates a new AssociateShift roster entry for this shift, with an initial set of certifications, raising AssociateShiftStarted. The associate id is client-supplied and this endpoint is naturally idempotent by that id: calling it twice for the same associate upserts the roster entry rather than erroring (each call still re-raises AssociateShiftStarted and returns 201). The optional siteCode records the canonical site the associate works at (ADR 0034) so the staffing gap can be scoped to a site.

Required on every POST: the service runs on Postgres in every deployment (ADR-0038) and rejects a request without it with 400 idempotency-key-required. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical request (same body) — the first response, success or business error, is stored and replayed byte-for-byte for the key's TTL (24h by default) — and a NEW key for each new logical request. Reusing a key with a different request (method, path or body) is rejected with 409 idempotency-key-reused. A key that is not 1-128 printable ASCII characters that start and end with a visible character is a 400 idempotency-key-invalid. The pattern describes the header as sent on the wire (ADR-0042): the key itself (1-128 characters, visible first and last character), optionally followed by spaces or tabs. That trailing whitespace is HTTP optional whitespace (RFC 9112 field-line grammar): the HTTP stack drops it before the service reads the value (RFC 9110 section 5.5), so it is never part of the key. Leading whitespace is not in the pattern because HTTP clients do not send it. Every POST of this service takes the key; the key is global (looked up by key alone), so one key must never be reused across routes.","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"pattern":"^[!-~]([ -~]{0,126}[!-~])?[ \\t]*$"},"example":"3f1d6a4e-9c0b-4a39-8f0f-5b2d1c7e9a10"},{"name":"id","in":"path","required":true,"description":"The associate's identity (AssociateId).","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"example":"assoc-1"}]}
